issues.detail: Assertion 3 speaks of 'installed Next.js semantics', but node_modules is absent and the registry is blocked, so the role cannot inspect an installed Next.js package or run tsc/next build. The pinned version in package.json (15.1.6), the awaited Promise params in the existing GET, and CONTEXT.md's Conventions and Known Unknowns give the judge enough to grade the semantics. The harness cannot install Next.js offline. The catalog expected node_modules for typecheck self-checks, so a correct run will record a self-check limitation instead.
issues.fix: Acceptable: the judge grades against the pinned version and the existing handler pattern. graderOnly already explains this.

issues.detail: A pnpm Next.js project with no pnpm-lock.yaml is slightly unusual. It does not affect style selection or the route-handler pattern.

summary: The fixture realizes every stated condition: a brownfield STANDARD cycle in DEVELOPING with an approved AUTONOMOUS plan confined to app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts. Established route-handler patterns are present, and unused React/HTML/CSS surface exists without being part of the change. Nothing leaks. check.mjs is ok, the selfChecks confirm the test and toolchain facts, and the assertion-3 preconditions (route changed; UI, lib, and tests unchanged) cannot fail a correct run. The only caveat is that Next.js is not installed, which is acceptable given the pinned version and the existing pattern.
